about: The shared definition of what Home is made of and the order it is drawn in,
for Mac, iOS, and web. Home is one screen on three surfaces, and the bug
this table exists to prevent is each surface keeping its own hardcoded stack:
a card the phone has and the browser lacks, or an order the Mac chose in
The person owns module order and visibility; `recent` is fixed last but
can be hidden from Settings > Home. The Worker stores it once
(`/api/home/preferences`) and every client reads the same answer.
rules: MODULES: the eight below, by stable id. Nothing else is a module: the clock
stays at the top and the version line at the bottom of every Home; the
Mac's WAITING ROOM is host state, drawn only while a room is being hosted,
and the Mac's destination buttons are chrome. A surface that has no way to
draw a module draws nothing for it and keeps its place in the order.
DEFAULT: the `modules` list, in that order, with each `enabledByDefault`.
VISIBLE: the enabled modules, in order, less any module `workModules` lists
while none of its work modules is on in the workspace (meet#990). No work
modules at all (an older Worker) draws every enabled module. Settings only
offers ungated modules, enabled or not. `visibleCases` pin Home; `offeredCases` pin Settings.
RESOLVE: given a stored list of {id, enabled}, keep the first occurrence of
each known id in stored order; drop unknown ids and later duplicates. A
module the stored list does not mention is inserted, walking the missing
ones in default order, after the nearest module that precedes it in the
default order and is present by then; when none is, at the front. It takes
its default `enabled`. A module with `canHide` false
is enabled whatever the stored list says. `recent` always moves to the
last module position, even when old or stored preferences put it earlier.
LEGACY: a stored `starred` module maps to `recent`. If both old ids are
stored, combine visibility with OR; its position is the final module
position, after all other modules. A stored `invitations` module (retired
2026-10-06: calendar invitations and events from email are INBOX sources)
is an unknown id and drops.
QUICK ACCESS (`recent`): one list combines owner-level starred rows and this device's
recent rows. Starred rows keep the starred endpoint's order and lead;
recent-only rows keep device recency order. Each kind/id appears once.
The recent source contributes at most eight rows; every resolved starred
row remains.
PLACEMENT: `recent` is the final card before the version line. It spans
both module columns in wide layouts and uses one column in narrow layouts.
Its shortcuts stay in one horizontal row and scroll when needed.
EMPTY: `enabled` decides whether a module may draw, never whether it has
anything to draw.
SHOW: whether a visible module draws once it has answered is
`showsEmpty` OR it has content (meet#1033). `showsEmpty` true: the room,
Quick Notes (the capture is the card) and Upcoming (the calendar state is
the card) draw empty. `showsEmpty` false: Inbox, Work, Commercial, Events
and Quick Access draw nothing when they have nothing to list. Content is
the rows the card would list: Inbox its unread conversations and INBOX
items, Work its overdue and due-today tasks, Commercial a summary, Events
an upcoming published event, Quick Access a starred or recent row. A
failed read is not content: the last known rows stand. No surface keeps
its own list of which cards draw empty. `showCases` pin it.
INBOX AND WORK: the `messages` module (titled Inbox) holds what is new:
unread conversations and every INBOX item, calendar invitations and events
from email among them, except unfiled Quick Notes (their
own module). The `work` module holds only what you already own: your
overdue and due-today tasks. A new thing never lands in Work.
INBOX ORDER: decisions and questions first, in the order the Worker gave;
then every other row, conversations and INBOX items alike, newest first.
Ties keep the order given. 'and N more' opens Work's INBOX.
COLUMNS: with two columns, `packColumns` assigns each module to one:
modules sorted tallest first (ties keep the person's order) go to the
shorter column, a module adds its height plus the gap; a module with no
height yet goes to the currently shorter column. The person's order is
kept inside each column. Every surface uses this packer with its own
measured heights. Once Home has settled, a placement holds while heights
change, so a late answer does not move a card, until the columns are
LOPSIDED: a card in the taller column, plus the gap, is at most half the
difference between the columns, so the taller column could give that card
away and still be the taller. A measured card with no column is lopsided
too. A lopsided Home packs again. A packer result is never lopsided, so a
repack is final until heights change. Quick Access is not packed: it sits
below.
DENSITY: `rows` is the most rows a list module draws before 'and N more',
and the number of placeholder rows it draws while it waits for its first
answer, so the wait and the answer are the same height. Every surface reads
it from here; none keeps its own count. `null` means the module is not a
capped list: notes measure their own page (`QuickNotePage`), commercial and
the agenda draw their own shapes, the room and quick access are fixed
furniture. The agenda's `home_following_rows` stays on
/api/calendar/preferences; only where Settings shows it moves.

cases.name: an empty list is the default too
stored order wins, and a hidden module stays in its place
a duplicate keeps its first position and first answer
a module the stored list predates lands after its default neighbour
a missing module with no present predecessor goes to the front
the retired invitations module drops and keeps no place
legacy starred folds into recent, pins it last, and combines visibility

packCases.name: tallest first to the shorter column, unmeasured to the shorter one
equal heights alternate in the person's order
three tall cards and two short ones split two against three

lopsidedCases.name: two short cards beside three tall ones are lopsided
a difference smaller than twice every taller card holds
a measured card with no column is lopsided
an unmeasured card does not count

recentMergeCases.name: starred rows lead, duplicates collapse by kind and id, and same-id different-kind rows remain

inboxOrderCases.name: invitations, decisions and questions lead in the given order; the rest is newest first
equal times keep the given order

visibleCases.name: every work module on draws every module
no events and no commercial work modules hide Events and Commercial
one commercial work module is enough for Commercial
an older Worker that names no work modules draws everything

showCases.name: a Home with nothing to list draws the room, Quick Notes and Upcoming
a Home with unread conversations and work due draws Inbox and Work first
every module with content draws every module

offeredCases.name: base workspace offers neither Events nor Commercial
Events on offers Events, not Commercial
a commercial work module offers Commercial, not Events
an older Worker offers every module
a disabled module is still offered in Settings

moveCases.name: moving Work down skips hidden Commercial and leaves it in place
moving Agenda down skips hidden Events and leaves it in place
moving Notes up skips hidden Commercial
the last offered module cannot move through Quick Access
an older Worker keeps the old adjacent move
a hidden disabled row keeps its saved visibility
